content_metadata.description: An analysis of a video recorded congressional hearing examining water management concerns and policy discrepancies, as well as diversity issues within the Interior Department.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the legislation introduced by Mr. Gallego?
When does Ms. Combs mention online training will be available for employees on diversity and inclusion?
What hand gesture does Mr. Gallego repeatedly use throughout the video?

qAndA.answer: The camera predominantly focuses on Mr. Gallego, the questioner, while Ms. Combs is often seen responding from a lower position, subtly emphasizing Mr. Gallego's authority.
qAndA.question: How does the video visually convey the power dynamic between Mr. Gallego and Ms. Combs?

qAndA.answer: The removal suggests potential hypocrisy within the Interior Department, where official statements about diversity might not be reflected in concrete actions and policies.
qAndA.question: What implicit message does the removal of 'gender' and 'sexual orientation' from the ethics guide send, despite Ms. Combs' statements about diversity and inclusion?

activities.description: Mr. Gallego discusses the issue of water carrying capacity loss due to subsidence in his district and mentions three major conveyance facilities.
Mr. Gallego asks about resources Interior is making available for conveyance and facility repairs.
Ms. Combs defers to Commissioner Burman for specifics, acknowledges the issue's importance, and promises information.
Mr. Gallego mentions the 'Move Water Now Act,' aimed at restoring water delivery.
Ms. Combs emphasizes efforts to find solutions for water movement and conveyance structures.
Mr. Gallego thanks Ms. Combs and promises to follow up.

Mr. Gallego acknowledges the statement, highlights the disconnect, and expresses hope for consistency.

text_to_speech: Thank you so much for being here Mrs. Combs. As my colleague Congressman Costa is saying, it's very dry out in California right now and those conditions pinpoint the need to have more storage to take advantage of wet years like last year. And I know that many of us are eagerly awaiting to see list of projects for Win Act Funding. Do you have a timeline when the Department plans to sending that list up to Congress? I think we're gonna make the deadline I think it's supposed to be made maybe next month. So we'll get back, I'll talk to reclamation, we will of course get you the list. When can we expect to Interior to start soliciting projects for actually for next year or is this just something that we do? Let me say that I will talk to Commissioner Berman and I know it's an important issue for you we will get back to you but I will talk to Commissioner Berman. Thanks so much and certainly in my district we have three major conveyance facilities. We have the Frank Kern Canal, the Delta Mendota Canal, and the California Aqueduct and these have all lost water carrying capacity because of subsidence. We're glad to see the department's made some this a priority to addressing these issues but can you talk more about the resources interest making their provision to make available for conveyance and the fixing of these facilities. With respect to the subsidence issue and the conveyance of water I know that there's a couple of options being looked at again that would defer to Commissioner Berman the question is you do you use the same path or not, I don't have the data on that but I understand it's critically important we will get that information to you. We're trying to work hand-in-hand with the Department you may know that I've introduced H.R.5316 - Move Water Now Act which is specifically which is targeted towards these conveyance facilities particularly the Frank Kern Canal. Carson, Costa, and I have another bill to address the Delta Mendota Canal and California Aqueduct very very important to what we need to be able to get water to where it's needed. Well obviously the movement of water is critical and the conveyance structures and infrastructures are critical and when you have a subsidence issue which of course you aware of the Friant Kern, we're trying to help with the state try to figure out a way to make it work, get it back operating. Thanks very much for that and we'll follow up on that. You know on another subject and I think my colleague Mr. Hughes from Colorado, made the point is that there seems to be a bit of a discrepancy or dichotomy with regard to the Land and Water Conservation Fund. Is this something that is supported by the agency? Yes in fact in my opening comments we stated that we did support it. I beg your pardon I was in an Ag committee meeting, but it seems and certainly the President the other day you know tweeted out the any comments of work of a couple senators protecting the the Conservation Fund for years to come but in his budget he's basically proposing to more or less eliminate it. Well, we support the administration's policy and we were given new direction yesterday. Well the policies is reflected in the hard numbers which is basically zero all right it's not zero but it's it's a fraction of what has been funded in the past. Well the president made clear his new direction yesterday and we are supporting that direction. Let's hope it doesn't change again. On an entirely different subject, it's very concerning that Interior removed the terms gender and sexual orientation from its 2017 ethics guide in preventing workplace discrimination against employees and replace them which is the single term sex. Since the Department of Interior was under no legal obligation to make this change, why did the Department remove sexual orientation and gender from its list of protected statuses? Well I don't have the information about that. I will tell you that Secretary Bernhardt has made it unequivocally clear that he is very supportive of diversity of all types in the Department which is why he authorized me to set up the workplace cultural diversity and counsel, and we worked very very hard on that and we'll be having a online training in about June by a vendor for all 65,000 employees on all of the issues you've raised whether it is gender, race, whatever it is going to be covered in every person in the Department will be required to take the training. We are very supportive of the appropriate, positive, inclusive culture at the Department. Thanks so much Mrs.Combs,  I'm out of time appreciate you being here.

youtube_description: On Wednesday March 4th, Rep. TJ Cox questioned Assistant Secretary of Policy, Management, and Budget, Susan Combs on the Department of the Interior’s spending priorities and the President Trump’s fiscal year 2021 budget proposal.
youtube_title: Rep. Cox at Examining DOI Spending Priorities and the President’s FY2021 Budget Proposal Hearing.
